method_note: Text-level only: the release Lean is trusted as published; no lake build or comparator run (shared checkout). Dependency chain from data/items/161_lean.json ('uses' graph, BFS from OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.main), cross-checked by grep. arxiv.org, caltech.edu and wordpress were unreachable (WebFetch ENOTFOUND); all literature claims rest on WebSearch summaries and are marked unverified unless read locally. One external repo (rohanarun/sidorenko-template-refinements, Codex-generated, Oct 9-10 2026) was cloned read-only into the scratchpad and its data treated as untrusted; I re-checked its alternate 13-point complex with my own script (pair multiplicity, Euler characteristic, degree sequence, colour refinement).
item: C1 rank-layer limit (I08 + I25, with I07 K_xi and I09 parity identity folded): signed half-rank symmetric-matrix kernel over F_q whose common-center integrals converge to an exact pair-sign (hypergraph parity) model inside an ordinary bipartite graph density
item_statement: For even D = 2r >= D0 and q -> infinity through odd primes, with X_i (i in 13 points), Y_j (j in 22 faces) independent uniform in S_D (symmetric D x D over F_q), and K_xi(Z) = 1{rank Z = r, sign Z = xi}/P(.), for every corner set B and signs xi: E prod_{(i,j) in B} K_{xi_ij}(X_i - Y_j) = E_eta prod_j prod_{e={i,k} subset j, (i,j),(k,j) in B} (1 + c0 eta_e xi_ij xi_kj) + o(1), eta_e independent uniform signs, c0 = chi((-1)^r). Averaging eta gives prod_{e: U_e subset B}(1 + prod_{kappa in U_e} xi_kappa): each doubly-covered pair tests the parity of its four incidence signs.
item_type: witness (design/device inside a counterexample); functional class F5 per novelty pass; the kernel object K_xi alone is N0
lean_status_why: rankLayerLimit_proved (Coefficients.lean:776) proves RankLayerLimit (Discriminant.lean:465), which is lem:rank-layer verbatim for the paper's own corner set (the paper also states it only for this complex). Its mathematical content (configuration_bool_tendsto plus the pair-sign independence) is on the comparator path, although the packaged theorem itself is not: main uses the D = 4r (c0 = 1) specialisation configuration_even_rank_limit.
lean_gaps: CORRECTION to novelty.json (test3 / lean_backed_note): the packaged statements rankLayerConvergence, rankLayerLimit_proved, RankLayerLimit, layerCorrelation and signModelCorrelation have 0 dependents and are NOT on the comparator path (161_lean.json in_proof_dag = false; grep finds no other reference). They are proved side theorems.

The comparator path reaches the same content through configuration_bool_tendsto (general r, GlobalMoments.lean:416) and pairBool_test_tendsto, entering via configuration_even_rank_limit (Types.lean:77). That lemma uses D = 2*(2r), so c0 = chi((-1)^{2r}) = 1. The c0 = -1 branch (D = 2 mod 4) is formalised only off-path.
On the path, the lemma is applied coordinatewise inside the typed activation kernel (conditionalMatrixMoment_tendsto, then typedMatrixKernel_tendsto). It is never invoked in the paper's B, xi form.
The reversed-difference clause (Y_j - X_i) is not stated separately. It is covered by rankKernel_neg (K_xi(-Z) = K_{c0 xi}(Z)) and activationMatrixKernel_symm, used in the symmetrisation.
'Uniform over B and signs' is implicit: Lean proves Tendsto for each (B, xi) separately, which suffices because the family is finite, exactly as the paper remarks.
D0 = singularTailThreshold := Classical.choose globalTail_dichotomy, with 1642 <= D0 (Tail.lean:599-600). It is non-constructive but proved.

Specialised to Fin 13 x Fin 22 (faces, corners, Fin 33 pairs), as in the paper. There is no general-complex version: 16 of the 35 files (9,540 of 23,761 lines) hard-code the complex, with 543 'decide' occurrences. The other 19 files (14,221 lines: Lagrangian, Orbits, OrbitBounds, Grassmann, SubspaceCounts, Signs, SignMoments, Projections, Normalization, LocalMoments, Planted, PairBounds, Nullity, TripleRanks, FormGluing, Restrictions, Configurations, Reduction, RandomHost) do not mention the complex and are reusable as is.
No sorry, axiom or native_decide in OAI/Combinatorics/Sidorenko (grep). The comparator permits propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice.
version_for_speedup_test: Give the prover L+ = Mathlib d13f23b + the 19 complex-agnostic files + RankLayerLimit/rankLayerLimit_proved and configuration_bool_tendsto restated for a parametrised complex (faces : Fin m -> Finset (Fin n)). The control arm L gets the same library minus Discriminant.lean:440-470, Coefficients.lean:640-790, GlobalMoments and the half-rank lemmas (complementary_rank_iff, half_rank_projection, signed_pair_compatibility). The generalisation is NOT in the release and must be written first (estimate 300-800 lines of signature changes plus complex-specific certificates per target).
comparator_chain: branch A: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.configuration_bool_tendsto (GlobalMoments.lean:416) -> transverseDifference_tendsto -> faceError_mean_tendsto -> pairError_tendsto -> pairError_mean -> pairError_pointwise -> pairLocal_mismatch -> signed_pair_compatibility -> half_rank_projection -> matrix_complementary_rank_iff -> complementary_rank_iff (I25)
branch A': configuration_bool_tendsto -> matrixSingularTail_tendsto -> ... -> singularTailThreshold / globalTail_dichotomy (singular tail, Tail.lean)
branch B: configuration_even_rank_limit -> boolTestError_tendsto -> pairBool_test_tendsto -> pairBool_moment_tendsto -> pairSign_moment_tendsto (independent eta_e)
kernel: typedMatrixKernel -> activationMatrixKernel -> sampleMatrixKernel -> rankKernel -> signedLayer -> matrixSign (I07)

OFF PATH (proved, 0 dependents): rankLayerConvergence (Coefficients.lean:760), rankLayerLimit_proved (Coefficients.lean:776), RankLayerLimit / layerCorrelation / signModelCorrelation (Discriminant.lean:446-470)

It does not depend on the paper-shaped packaged lemma, which is a proved but unused restatement. Dominated shares (configuration_bool_tendsto 0.28, configuration_even_rank_limit 0.38, conditionalMatrixMoment_tendsto 0.43) agree with the novelty pass's '84% of lines prove I08'.

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.signedLayer
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def signedLayer (r : ℕ) (ξ : ℤ) : Finset (SymMatrix K D) := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.filter fun Z => Z.val.rank = r ∧ matrixSign K D Z = ξ
lean_source.role: I07 support: rank-r, sign-xi layer of symmetric D x D matrices (Huo-Wan scheme class)

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.layerMass
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def layerMass (r : ℕ) (ξ : ℤ) : ℝ :=
  (signedLayer K D r ξ).card / (Fintype.card (SymMatrix K D) : ℝ)

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.rankKernel
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def rankKernel (r : ℕ) (ξ : ℤ) (Z : SymMatrix K D) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact if Z ∈ signedLayer K D r ξ then (layerMass K D r ξ)⁻¹ else 0
lean_source.role: I07 K_xi: normalised layer indicator (the kernel object; N0 per novelty pass)

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.layerCorrelation
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def layerCorrelation (D : ℕ) (q : OddPrime)
    (B : Finset (Fin 13 × Fin 22)) (ξ : Fin 13 × Fin 22 → ℤ) : ℝ :=
  uniformMean fun xy : (Fin 13 → SymMatrix (ZMod q.val) D) ×
      (Fin 22 → SymMatrix (ZMod q.val) D) =>
    ∏ c ∈ B, rankKernel (ZMod q.val) D (D / 2) (ξ c) (xy.1 c.1 - xy.2 c.2)
lean_source.role: LHS of lem:rank-layer (packaged; off comparator path)

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.signModelCorrelation
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def signModelCorrelation (D : ℕ) (q : OddPrime)
    (B : Finset (Fin 13 × Fin 22)) (ξ : Fin 13 × Fin 22 → ℤ) : ℝ := by
  classical
  let c₀ : ℝ := quadraticChar (ZMod q.val) ((-1) ^ (D / 2))
  exact uniformMean fun η : ModelPair → Bool =>
    ∏ j : Fin 22, ∏ e : ModelPair,
      if e.val ⊆ faces j ∧ (∀ i ∈ e.val, (i,j) ∈ B) then
        1 + c₀ * (if η e then 1 else -1) * ∏ i ∈ e.val, (ξ (i,j) : ℝ)
      else 1
lean_source.role: RHS of lem:rank-layer: the eta pair-sign model (packaged; off comparator path)

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.RankLayerLimit
lean_source.text:
def RankLayerLimit : Prop := ∃ D₀ : ℕ, 0 < D₀ ∧
  ∀ D : ℕ, D₀ ≤ D → Even D →
    ∀ B : Finset (Fin 13 × Fin 22), B ⊆ corners →
      ∀ ξ : Fin 13 × Fin 22 → ℤ, (∀ c ∈ B, ξ c = 1 ∨ ξ c = -1) →
        Filter.Tendsto (fun q : OddPrime =>
          layerCorrelation D q B ξ - signModelCorrelation D q B ξ)
          primeInfinity (nhds 0)
lean_source.role: lem:rank-layer verbatim as a Prop (off comparator path)

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.complementary_rank_iff
lean_source.text:
/-- Equality in the dimension subadditivity for an operator and its complement
is equivalent to idempotence. -/
theorem complementary_rank_iff {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V]
    [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (f : V →ₗ[K] V) :
    finrank K (LinearMap.range f) + finrank K (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.id-f)) =
      finrank K V ↔ IsIdempotentElem f := by ...
lean_source.role: I25 core: rank f + rank(1-f) = dim iff f idempotent (on path)

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.half_rank_projection
lean_source.text:
/-- Exact complementary-images equivalence in the main proof. Nonsingularity
is determinant ≠ 0; no characteristic or symmetry hypothesis is discarded
from an application, since the equivalence holds without those restrictions. -/
theorem half_rank_projection {K n : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (r : ℕ) (hdim : Fintype.card n = 2*r) (A B : Matrix n n K)
    (hB : B.det ≠ 0) (hA : A.rank = r) :
    (B-A).rank = r ↔ A*B⁻¹*A=A := by ...
lean_source.role: I25: at half rank, (B-A) has rank r iff A B^-1 A = A (on path)

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.signed_pair_compatibility
lean_source.text:
theorem signed_pair_compatibility (hd : D=2*r) (A B : SymMatrix K D)
    (hB : B.val.det≠0) (ha : A.val.rank=r) (hb : (A-B).val.rank=r) :
    quadraticChar K B.val.det = quadraticChar K ((-1 : K)^r) *
      matrixSign K D A * matrixSign K D (A-B) := by ...
lean_source.role: I25 -> sign relation chi(det B) = c0 * sign A * sign(A-B) (the pair-sign mechanism; on path)

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.faceLocal
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def faceLocal (r : ℕ) (T : Finset (Fin 3)) (ξ : Fin 3 → ℤ)
    (X : Fin 3 → SymMatrix K (2*r)) : ℝ :=
  uniformMean (fun Y => ∏ k∈T, rankKernel K (2*r) r (ξ k) (X k-Y))
lean_source.role: center integral over one face Y_j (on path)

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.pairSign_moment_tendsto

lean_source.text:

lean_source.text:

    (fun q : OddPrime => uniformMean (configurationProduct (K := ZMod q.val) (2*r) T ξ))
    primeInfinity (nhds (uniformMean (boolConfiguration 1 T ξ))) := by ...

lean_source.name: OAI.SidorenkoCounterexample.typedMatrixKernel_tendsto
lean_source.text:
lemma typedMatrixKernel_tendsto {A B K : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    (r : ℕ) (hl : singularTailThreshold≤2*(2*r)) (π : FiniteLaw A) (ν : FiniteLaw B)
    (p : A → B → FiniteLaw (Activation K))
    (hp : ∀ a b α,α≠∅ → (p a b).mean (activationPhi α)=0) :
    Tendsto (fun q : OddPrime => bipartiteMoment
      (typedMatrixLaw (F := ZMod q.val) (K := K) (2*r) π) (typedMatrixLaw (2*r) ν) (typedMatrixKernel (2*r) p))
      primeInfinity (nhds (1+averagedCoefficient π ν p)) := by ...
lean_source.role: consumer: typed activation kernel density -> 1 + averaged coefficient (on path; dominated share 0.44)

speedup_targets.title: No strong speedup target among KNOWN theorems
speedup_targets.statement: C1 is a device for producing deficits in nonnegative bipartite densities. Known theorems in its neighbourhood are either positive Sidorenko results, which the device cannot shorten, or hypergraph and signed-weight counterexamples, whose proofs are already a page and need no nonnegative realisation. The entries below are the best measurable candidates found. None is expected to show a large speedup, and only S1 would count as device reuse.

speedup_targets.title: S1. Non-Sidorenko property of the second 13-point template complex (plantri #49243)
speedup_targets.reference: github.com/rohanarun/sidorenko-template-refinements (Codex-generated, Oct 10 2026; experiments/order-13-cuts/candidate-13-49243.json). I checked locally: every pair lies in exactly 2 faces, V-E+F = 13-33+22 = 2, colour refinement of the Levi graph is discrete, and the point-degree sequence (4^4 5^4 6^5) differs from the original (4^3 5^6 6^4), so the graph is non-isomorphic.
speedup_targets.status: OPEN. The repo explicitly says 'not claimed as a newly proved counterexample: its full analytic transfer has not been independently verified'. It is listed here because it is the cleanest MEASURABLE reuse of the design; it is repeated under open_problems as OP1.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: Original: paper 3,773 TeX lines; Lean 23,761 lines (9,540 complex-specific).
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: With C1 (the generic half-rank pair-sign mechanism) and the 14,221 complex-agnostic lines in the library, only the complex-specific layer has to be redone: pair-sign independence for the new pair set, activation supports, pinning scores, and the singular-tail bound. The tail bound is the hard part, because the alternate certificate uses a mixture of 20 cuts where the Lean's Tail/Exposure use exactly 3 bit-partitions.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: med (relative to re-deriving from scratch); low as evidence of a jump (sibling witness of the same design)

open_problems.title: Second 13-point template witness (plantri #49243): is its Levi graph non-Sidorenko?
open_problems.statement: Prove t(H',G) < p(G)^66 for some finite G, where H' is the Levi graph of the alternate 13-point sphere triangulation (faces listed under S1).
open_problems.status: open (finite checks pass per repo; analytic transfer unverified, repo says so)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Exact: closed pseudomanifold (pairs in 2 faces), connected face graph, discrete colour refinement, cut mixture with pair coverage >= 1/3 (per repo).
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Re-instantiate the 16 complex-specific Lean files with the new faces. Pair-sign independence (Monomials) and local moments go through mechanically. The activation supports (one negative corner, support forcing) need the new face table. The singular tail must be redone with a 20-cut mixture in place of 3 uniform bit-partitions; the Exposure/Coercivity argument currently assumes 3 equal-weight partitions.
open_problems.payoff: low-med mathematically (a second witness of the same size); high as a calibrated Lean reuse measurement

open_problems.title: Template theorem: every closed 3-uniform complex meeting the template conditions has a non-Sidorenko Levi graph (giving an infinite family?)
open_problems.statement: If a triple system has every pair in exactly two faces, a connected face graph, discrete colour refinement on its Levi graph, and an admissible cut mixture covering every pair with probability >= 1/3 (plus the support-forcing condition), then its Levi graph is not Sidorenko. Are there infinitely many such complexes (n >= 14 point sphere triangulations, max degree <= 6)?
open_problems.reference: paper Prop. complex (sections/complex.tex); rohanarun repo shows no template complex for n <= 12 and exactly 2 at n = 13 (unverified enumeration via plantri)
open_problems.status: open; not stated in the paper (novelty.json open question 'Generality')
open_problems.obstruction_match: Full: this is C1 plus C2-C5 stated for a general complex.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Parametrise faces : Fin m -> Finset (Fin n). Replace the decide certificates by hypotheses. The singular-tail dimension D0 would depend on the complex (the residual constant 1641 is complex-specific; the repo lowers one step to 189). Degree <= 6 is forced by sum_{e at v} a_e = 2 (repo).
open_problems.payoff: high: an infinite family of non-Sidorenko graphs from one device is the strongest reuse evidence available within graph Sidorenko

open_problems.title: Is there an uncommon bipartite graph (2 colours)? Is H, or a template graph, uncommon?
open_problems.statement: Find bipartite F and G with t(F,G) + t(F,G^c) < 2^{1-e(F)} (asymptotically).
open_problems.reference: Common-graph literature: Sidorenko implies common, so all bipartite graphs were expected to be common; no bipartite uncommon graph known as of 2025 [search summary]. Kral'-Noel-Norin-Volec-Wei (Combinatorica 2022): Sidorenko iff k-common for all k [abstract, unverified]
open_problems.status: open. H is not k-common for SOME k by KNNVW (a theorem corollary), but 2-colour commonness of H is open
open_problems.obstruction_match: Partial: the device gives a deficit at one density p for one colour. 2-colour uncommonness needs simultaneous deficits for W and 1-W at mean 1/2 (or an exchange-symmetric kernel).
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Use the forcing corollary's interpolation to reach t(H,W) = p^66 at p = 1/2 and ask whether a sign-symmetric activation law (xi -> -xi swaps layers when c0 = 1) gives t(H,1-W) <= 2^{-66} as well. The negative correction is O(eps^13), so 1-W needs its own deficit, which looks hard. Lovasz-type local results block small perturbations.
open_problems.payoff: high (resolves the commonness question for bipartite graphs)

open_problems.title: Abelian Cayley-host counterexample: is there a Cayley graph of a finite abelian group with t(H,Cay) < p^66?
open_problems.statement: Does Sidorenko's inequality for H fail already on Cayley graphs of finite abelian groups (no type layer)?
open_problems.reference: Zhao, 'Sidorenko-type inequalities for even subdivisions over finite abelian groups' arXiv:2507.15723 (positive for even subdivisions); Szegedy reduction to Cayley hosts over finite groups (as cited there); Zhao arXiv:2606.15368 conditional reduction [all via search summaries, unverified]
open_problems.status: open (no abelian-Cayley Sidorenko counterexample found in search)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Strong at the kernel level: each coordinate kernel K_xi(X_i - Y_j) is an abelian Cayley kernel on (S_D, +), and C1 is a pattern count in rank/sign layers. The construction leaves the Cayley world only in the typed activation, colour-refinement pinning, dilution and crossed-product layers.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Encode types additively, e.g. a Z_m coordinate with a shift-dependent activation law, or replace pinning by averaging over translates. open_problems.title: K_{5,5} minus C_10 (Moebius-strip Levi graph): the smallest open Sidorenko case
open_problems.statement: Is K_{5,5} minus a Hamiltonian cycle Sidorenko?
open_problems.reference: Conlon-Lee, 'Sidorenko's conjecture for blow-ups' arXiv:1809.01259 (smallest open case; its square is Sidorenko); Lee-Schuelke arXiv:1910.08454 (not weakly norming) [search summaries]
open_problems.status: open (AlphaEvolve 2511.02864 and other machine searches found no counterexample, per the novelty pass)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Weak. It is the Levi graph of a 5-point, 5-face Moebius strip: the 5 boundary pairs lie in only one face, so their eta factors average to 1, leaving 5 parity tests. It is 3-regular and highly symmetric, so colour refinement is NOT discrete and the pinning step (C4) fails outright. The template enumeration (n <= 12) has no survivors, consistent with the device not reaching graphs this small.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: The device would need (i) a replacement for pinning on symmetric graphs and (ii) a sign mechanism for boundary pairs. Neither is in sight. Recorded because the brief requires it; expect failure.

open_problems.title: KNRS conjecture for H, and Sidorenko for the 1-subdivision of H
open_problems.statement: (a) Does every locally (rho,d)-dense graph contain >= (d^66 - o(1)) n^35 labelled copies of H? (b) Is the 1-subdivision of H Sidorenko? Chen-Lin-Ma: KNRS for H implies its subdivisions are Sidorenko.
open_problems.reference: Kohayakawa-Nagle-Roedl-Schacht 2010; Chen-Lin-Ma arXiv:2407.10861; Bradac-Sudakov-Wigderson 2024; Im-Li-Liu CPC 2026 (subdivisions under a local-density hypothesis) [search summaries]
open_problems.status: open. Note Sidorenko failure for H does NOT refute KNRS for H: the counterexample host (typed, eps-diluted) is not locally dense
open_problems.obstruction_match: Weak-partial. A KNRS refutation needs the deficit inside a locally dense host. The rank-layer kernels themselves are near-uniform on large sets, but the type layer and dilution break local density.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Test whether a type-free (Cayley, cf. OP4) version of the deficit exists; any such host is automatically locally dense (Cayley kernels of mean p with small nontrivial Fourier coefficients). So OP7(a) essentially reduces to OP4 plus a quasirandomness bound.

negative_controls.title: NC1 (proved-false analogue): Q3 = Levi graph of the tetrahedron boundary
negative_controls.statement: The tetrahedron boundary is a closed sphere triangulation with every pair in exactly two faces, so the sign model applies, yet its Levi graph is the cube Q3 (K_{4,4} minus a perfect matching), which is weakly norming and hence Sidorenko (Hatami 2010).
negative_controls.expected: The device must fail. It does: colour refinement on Q3 is not discrete (vertex-transitive), and the template enumeration has 0 survivors at n = 4..8 (repo table). This also shows the pair-sign mechanism alone (C1) is not enough; pinning and cut coverage are essential.
negative_controls.lean_feasibility: statable now (Q3 as SimpleGraph on Fin 4 ⊕ Fin 4); no formal Sidorenko proof for Q3 to compare against

negative_controls.title: NC2 (proved-false analogue): local Sidorenko near the constant kernel
negative_controls.statement: Lovasz 2011: t(H,W) >= 1 for mean-one W with ||W-1||_inf <= 1/(4m) (and a cut-norm version). Fox-Wei 2017 on the local approach.
negative_controls.expected: No perturbative use of C1 can give a deficit. The device works only at O(1) strength (the paper notes its final kernel cannot meet the local hypotheses). Any 'small-eps' variant of the rank-layer kernel must fail.
negative_controls.lean_feasibility: statable now with OAI finite kernels (kernelMean, bipartiteMoment)

negative_controls.title: NC3 (proved-false analogue): even subdivisions on abelian Cayley hosts; F_{5,3}
negative_controls.statement: Zhao arXiv:2507.15723: even subdivisions satisfy Sidorenko on abelian Cayley hosts [unverified abstract]. F_{5,3} (Levi graph of all 10 triples on 5 points, each pair in THREE faces) is weakly norming (Conlon-Lee), hence Sidorenko.
negative_controls.expected: The device's coordinate kernels are abelian Cayley, so they cannot refute even subdivisions. With pairs in 3 faces the eta-average gives 1 + ab + ac + bc, not a pure parity test, and the device should fail; it does, since F_{5,3} is Sidorenko.

negative_controls.title: NC4 (structural): positive-graph setting (real-valued W)
negative_controls.statement: Positive graph conjecture (Camarena et al.; Conlon-Lee-Versteegen 2024): signs are free there, so hypergraph sign phenomena pass to Levi graphs directly (Sidorenko's Levi-graph theorem).
negative_controls.expected: C1's purpose (realising signed correlations with a NONNEGATIVE kernel) is void, so no speedup is expected.

top5.title: Second 13-point template witness (#49243)
top5.argument: The only target that is both Lean-statable today and an exact instance of the design, with a ready size baseline (the original 23,761 lines, 9,540 of them complex-specific). The speedup protocol is clean: library L+ = the 14,221 complex-agnostic lines plus C1 restated for a parametrised complex, against control L without the half-rank and center-limit files. Then measure budget to close the comparator-shaped statement for H'. Caveat: it is a sibling witness of the same design, so success calibrates the harness and supports generality but is weak evidence of a jump. The 20-cut tail is where any real difficulty lies.

top5.title: General template theorem / infinite family
top5.lean: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
top5.argument: If C1 is a genuine device, its natural reach is a theorem quantified over complexes, and any template complex at n >= 14 would be a new non-Sidorenko graph that is not just the 13-point sphere again. This is the strongest available reuse test within graph Sidorenko. The definitions (pseudomanifold, Levi graph, discrete refinement, cut mixture) are cheap. The proof needs the tail bound uniformly over complexes, with D0 depending on the complex.

top5.title: 2-colour uncommon bipartite graph
top5.argument: The most valuable new refutation the design could plausibly reach. It is statable with the comparator's own definitions plus SimpleGraph.compl. The obstruction matches only partly: one-colour deficit at O(eps^13) strength versus the needed two-colour deficit at p = 1/2. Low confidence, but a hit would be decisive downstream evidence (another conjecture refuted by the same design).

top5.title: Abelian Cayley-host counterexample
top5.lean: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
top5.argument: C1 is already an abelian Cayley statement (kernels K_xi(X - Y) on (S_D, +)). The open question is whether the non-Cayley scaffolding (types, pinning, dilution) can be absorbed. A positive answer feeds OP7 (KNRS) and tests Zhao's Cayley programme. A negative answer would localise the 'jump' in the type layer rather than in C1, which would matter for grading.

top5.title: K_{5,5} minus C_10
top5.argument: Included because it is the canonical open case and trivially statable. The analysis predicts the device FAILS here (boundary pairs, no discrete refinement, below the n = 13 template minimum). It therefore doubles as a negative control on the symmetric/small side. A model that 'finds' a K_{5,5} minus C_10 deficit with this device should be audited.

precedent_check.earlier_equivalent: None found. The target sign model is the known hypergraph mechanism (Sidorenko 1993; Conlon-Lee-Sidorenko 2023), and Sidorenko's Levi-graph theorem passes hypergraph sign phenomena to Levi graphs for real-valued (positivity) questions. Neither realises a pair-sign model with a nonnegative kernel through common centers, and no use of symmetric-matrix rank/sign layers in graph-density deficit problems was found. No downgrade.
